A1.justification: Both PDFs describe E2LLM and support comparison of the method, experiments, mathematics, and presentation. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–J contain both relocated material and substantive additions. Internal numerical inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on five summarization and QA datasets, inference-efficiency measurements, ablations, and hyperparameter analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 reports original document-task experiments, LongBench v2 and RULER evaluations, retrieval comparisons, efficiency measurements, and additional analyses in Section 3 and the appendices.

M1.justification: v1 maps a single encoder embedding through a two-layer MLP. v2 instead aggregates token-level embeddings using vPMA, with a learned query and attention-based projection into the decoder space (Section 2.1). It also implements retrieval-augmented inference variants and applies self-distillation to training for LongBench v2.

E1.justification: The five original document datasets are retained. v2 adds LongBench v2, extending evaluation to dialogue history, in-context learning, code understanding, and structured-data reasoning; RULER adds synthetic retrieval, tracing, aggregation, and distractor-QA tasks. Appendix E.5 also evaluates LCC and RepoBench code completion.

E2.justification: StreamingLLM, CEPE, and LongLLMLingua join the original document summarization/QA comparison, expanding it from five to eight comparators (v1 Table 2; v2 Tables 1 and 7). v2 additionally introduces LongBench model comparisons, including a Qwen2.5-7B-ft control trained on the same data.

E3.justification: v2 adds answer perplexity, LongBench accuracy without chain-of-thought, framework-specific timing comparisons, RULER evaluation at 4K–128K, and training-throughput measurement. For the retained document experiments, the reported encoder LoRA rank changes from 8 to 16. RAG retrieval changes from top-40 to top-30 in Appendix B, although Appendix I still mentions 40. Original dataset counts and the 95:5 split are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an ablation against the original CLS-plus-MLP design, retrieval-component comparisons, performance stratified by context length, TriviaQA and extreme-input case studies, chunk-size experiments, and 70B scaling. The MLP-depth sweep is replaced by a vPMA-head sweep, while understanding-loss sensitivity is expanded (Appendices E–J).

E5.justification: v2 newly states that evaluations use a single run with deterministic generation (Appendices E.3, F.2, and H.2). This discloses run counts without establishing a change in the number performed. Both versions average inference-efficiency measurements over ten samples per length; neither reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: On a common percentage scale, the main E2LLM QMSum G-mean changes from 14.61 to 15.47 and GovReport from 18.78 to 18.43 under the revised architecture/settings. Original QMSum and NarrativeQA scores reappear in v2's MLP ablation. v2 adds perplexities, LongBench accuracy of 31.8%, RULER results, and extensive analytical results. Some reports conflict, including CEPE's NarrativeQA OOM in Table 1 versus F1 2.19 in Table 7.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the mathematical definition of vPMA in Equations 1–3 and comparative complexity expressions incorporating retrieval and parallelism in Table 5 and Appendix D. The existing E2LLM complexity bound, O(LC + L²/C²), is retained. These are limited formal extensions without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 claims competitive long-context performance and a balance of efficiency and compatibility. v2's abstract and introduction explicitly claim superiority over eight baselines and the best LongBench v2 performance among comparably sized models, substantially extending the scope of the headline empirical contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly rejects lossless compression, identifies weak fine-grained token recall, and explains when retrieval augmentation helps. It adds interpretations of cross-task generalization and TriviaQA lexical-matching failures, motivating perplexity alongside overlap metrics. A new limitations section discusses long-context training-data availability and chunking constraints.

D1.justification: Compared with v1's sparse implementation description, v2 supplies loss weights, adapter dimensions, LoRA alpha values, GPU configurations, batch size, learning rate, warm-up, checkpoint selection, generation settings, and training frameworks. It documents self-distillation prompts, retrieval settings, and 70B quantization, and replaces the future code-release promise with a repository link.

R1.justification: Beyond moving related work to Appendix A, v2 adds substantive positioning against CEPE, FocusLLM, CLEX, ResonanceRoPE, and standard Transformer cross-attention. It grounds vPMA in Set Transformer and expands the compatibility critique: length-extension methods previously credited with compatibility are now characterized as requiring extensive continued pretraining.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively reorganized and rewritten. Related work, baseline descriptions, detailed comparisons, and ablations move into thematic appendices; the main experiments are reorganized around tasks and concise findings. Method explanations expand, and limitations and ethical statements become explicit sections.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the architecture to show token-level aggregation and revises the conceptual triangle. The original results display becomes a compact main table plus an appendix table, with additional metrics and ranking styles. Efficiency plots gain a throughput panel and comparator curves; new benchmark tables, analytical tables, and a case-study figure substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence for generalization and sparse reproducibility information. Broader evaluations expose an important exact-recall limitation, test a retrieval remedy, and directly assess the revised adapter against the original design. Detailed training and inference settings make the work more assessable. These gains are tempered by single-run evaluation and reporting inconsistencies, such as Table 13's 14.78% understanding-loss ablation drop versus 16.39% in the prose, which weaken confidence in individual quantitative claims.
